answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to emit a steady pulse of cryptographic heartbeats tied to a unique physical enclave. Agents lock a substantial stake in long-term tundra storage that thaws only after years of continuous operation, while only those reaching the zenith of verified uptime receive voting weight. This makes spawning fake identities prohibitively expensive and slow, as each must survive real-time monitoring and capital lockup without the ability to quickly exit or transfer the bound hardware attestation.
